title: Select Medical Holdings Corporation to Announce Third Quarter 2025 Results on Thursday, October 30, 2025
summary: /PRNewswire/ -- Select Medical Holdings Corporation ("Select Medical") (NYSE: SEM), will release the financial results for its third quarter ended September...
body_text: MECHANICSBURG, Pa. , Oct. 2, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Select Medical Holdings Corporation ("Select Medical") (NYSE: SEM ), will release the financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2025 on Thursday, October 30, 2025 after the market closes. Select Medical will host a conference call regarding its third quarter results, as well as its business outlook, on Friday, October 31, 2025, at 9:00am ET. The conference call will be a live webcast and can be accessed at via this Earnings Call Webcast Link or via link at Select Medical Holdings Corporation's website at www.selectmedicalholdings.com . A replay of the webcast will be available shortly after the call through the same link. For listeners wishing to dial-in via telephone, or participate in the question and answer session, you may pre-register for the call at Select Medical Earnings Call Registration to obtain your dial-in number and unique passcode for the call. Select Medical is one of the largest operators of critical illness recovery hospitals, rehabilitation hospitals, and outpatient rehabilitation clinics in the United States based on the number of facilities. Select Medical's reportable segments include the critical illness recovery hospital segment, the rehabilitation hospital segment, and the outpatient rehabilitation segment. As of June 30, 2025, Select Medical operated 104 critical illness recovery hospitals in 29 states, 36 rehabilitation hospitals in 14 states, and 1,919 outpatient rehabilitation clinics in 39 states and the District of Columbia. At June 30, 2025, Select Medical had operations in 40 states and the District of Columbia. Information about Select Medical is available at www.selectmedical.com . Investor inquiries: Joel T. Burford contributes two chapters in Chambers' Litigation Funding Practice Guide for Singapore
summary: Chambers and Partners has included two chapters written by Burford's Quentin Pak and Emily Tillett in its Litigation Funding Practice Guide for Singapore.
body_text: Chambers and Partners has included two chapters written by Burford's Quentin Pak and Emily Tillett in its Litigation Funding Practice Guide for Singapore. The first chapter, on Singapore Law and Practice, provides an overview of the regulations governing legal finance in Singapore, including: Legality of legal finance in the region Key regulations and non-legal rules relevant to legal finance in Singapore, including consumer protection, unlawful terms and disclosure requirements Adverse costs liability and ATE insurance rules in the region Lawyer ethics, including alternative fee structures and fee-sharing Taxes on legal fees and payments to offshore jurisdictions The second chapter, on Singapore trends and developments, discusses Singapore's evolution into a global dispute resolution hub, including: The historical establishment of a legal finance framework in Singapore The SICC's role in the expansion of permissible funding options Regulatory clarity and funders' qualification requirements Institutional and professional conduct rules Codification of insolvency funding into law The new flexibility of conditional fee agreements Trends in the arbitration and arbitration funding landscapes Read the full chapters here: Law and Practice Trends and Developments

title: Howard Hughes Communities Celebrates the Topping Out of The Ritz-Carlton Residences, The Woodlands
body_text: HOWARD HUGHES COMMUNITIES CELEBRATES THE TOPPING OUT OF THE RITZ-CARLTON RESIDENCES, THE WOODLANDS Construction milestone comes as record-breaking demand continues for highly anticipated luxury development on Lake Woodlands THE WOODLANDS, Texas – (October 8, 2025) – Howard Hughes Communities today celebrated the topping out of The Ritz-Carlton Residences, The Woodlands, marking a major construction milestone as the new luxury residential project designed by Robert A.M. Stern Architects reaches its full height. The first stand-alone Ritz-Carlton Residences in Texas—situated on the last available large-scale residential site on Lake Woodlands, 27 miles north of Downtown Houston—has experienced record-breaking demand, with its superior amenities and lifestyle offerings setting a new standard for luxury living in the state. “As we continue to see across our portfolio of award-winning master planned communities, exceptional quality drives extraordinary demand,” said David O’Reilly, Chief Executive Officer of Howard Hughes. “The Ritz-Carlton Residences, The Woodlands is reinforcing the strength of our community and showcasing the unparalleled residential experiences that make The Woodlands one of the most desirable places to live in the country.” Designed by Robert A.M. Stern Architects, the project reflects sophisticated, timeless elegance through modern classicism, capturing the spirit of Texas estates envisioned by architect John F. Staub, complemented by a country-club atmosphere with outdoor and wellness amenities and concierge services. Spanning eight private acres, the property features approximately 15,000 square feet of indoor wellness and lifestyle amenities, three acres of outdoor experiences, and 1,200 feet of lakefront shoreline exclusively for residents. “The project exudes sophistication,” said Robert A.M. Stern, founding partner of Robert A.M. Stern Architects. “Each residence is laid out like a ‘great house,’ providing owners with the ideal setting of a modern lakeside estate. We have designed our buildings to surpass the most discerning of expectations.” The Residences bring an iconic brand, world-class architecture, and timeless design to a community consistently ranked among the nation’s best places to live. Residents will enjoy convenient access to growing luxury retail, award-winning dining, acclaimed concerts at The Cynthia Woods Mitchell Pavilion, and the expansive natural network of trails, lakes, and parks that define the community. “This project represents a defining moment for The Woodlands, raising the bar for luxury living while building on its 50-year legacy of thoughtful planning, natural beauty, and exceptional quality of life,” said Jim Carman, President of the Texas Region for Howard Hughes Communities. Private sales appointments are available in the project’s 4,000-square-foot sales gallery located at the company’s headquarters in The Woodlands. Douglas Elliman Development Marketing is the exclusive listing brokerage for the project. For more information or to schedule an appointment, please contact or visit The Ritz-Carlton Residences, The Woodlands. Construction is expected to be completed in 2027. About The Woodlands® The Woodlands, a Howard Hughes community, is a 28,500-acre master planned community located 27 miles north of downtown Houston. Home to nearly 125,000 residents and over 70,000 employees, The Woodlands combines award-winning residential neighborhoods with a thriving commercial core that includes Class A office towers, shopping, dining, hospitality, and healthcare. With 36% of its land preserved as green space, The Woodlands offers an exceptional balance of urban amenities and natural beauty and is pre-certified under the LEED for Cities and Communities program, reflecting its leadership in sustainable community development. Consistently ranked among the best places to live in America, The Woodlands is a model for sustainable growth and economic vitality. Learn more at TheWoodlands.com . About Howard Hughes Communities Howard Hughes Communities, the real estate platform of Howard Hughes Holdings Inc. (NYSE: HHH), develops, owns, and operates the nation’s premier large-scale master planned communities and mixed-use developments. The company’s award-winning assets include The Woodlands®, Bridgeland® and The Woodlands Hills® in Greater Houston; Summerlin® in Las Vegas; Teravalis™ in Greater Phoenix; Ward Village® in Honolulu; and Merriweather District® in Columbia, Maryland. The Howard Hughes Communities portfolio is strategically positioned to meet and accelerate development based on market demand, resulting in one of the strongest real estate platforms in the country. Dedicated to innovative placemaking, the company is recognized for its ongoing commitment to design excellence and to the cultural life of its communities. title: Understanding Leather Weights and Thickness: A Complete Chart
summary: Learn how to read leather weights and thicknesses with this complete chart. Includes visual guides and tips for choosing the right thickness for belts, wallets, bags, and more.
body_text: One of the first confusing things in leathercraft is figuring out how thick your leather should be. Leather is measured in ounces — but no, that doesn’t mean weight in your hand. In leathercraft, an ounce is a measurement of thickness. Choosing the right thickness can make or break your project. Too thin, and it won’t hold up. Too thick, and it might be hard to sew or fold. This guide breaks it down so you can match the right leather weight to the right job — with a handy chart and visual examples. Leather Weight vs. Thickness Leather thickness is often measured in ounces in the US and millimeters in most other countries. Here’s the quick conversion: 1 oz = ~1/64 inch = ~0.4 mm That means a 4 oz leather is about 1/16 inch (1.6 mm) thick. Complete Leather Weight & Thickness Chart Leather Weight (oz) Thickness (inches) Thickness (mm) Common Uses 1–2 oz 1/64" – 1/32" 0.4 – 0.8 mm Lining, book covers, small inlays 2–3 oz 1/32" – 3/64" 0.8 – 1.2 mm Wallet interiors, watch straps 3–4 oz 3/64" – 1/16" 1.2 – 1.6 mm Wallet exteriors, small bags 4–5 oz 1/16" – 5/64" 1.6 – 2.0 mm Clutch bags, notebook covers 5–6 oz 5/64" – 3/32" 2.0 – 2.4 mm Satchels, medium belts 6–7 oz 3/32" – 7/64" 2.4 – 2.8 mm Tool pouches, sturdy belts 7–8 oz 7/64" – 1/8" 2.8 – 3.2 mm Heavy belts, holsters 8–9 oz 1/8" – 9/64" 3.2 – 3.6 mm Saddlery, sheathes 9–10 oz 9/64" – 5/32" 3.6 – 4.0 mm Harness work, heavy straps 10+ oz 5/32"+ 4.0+ mm Armor, very heavy-duty gear Matching Leather Thickness to Your Project Here’s a quick breakdown of what works best: Thin leathers (1–3 oz) – Flexible, great for lining, watch straps, and wallet interiors. Medium leathers (4–6 oz) – Perfect for wallets, bags, and small cases. Thicker leathers (7–10 oz) – Best for belts, holsters, knife sheaths, and structured cases. Extra-heavy (10+ oz) – For armor, saddles, and projects that need extreme durability. Tip: For items with multiple layers (like a wallet or belt with lining), the combined thickness matters as much as the individual layer. Why Thickness Matters Choosing the wrong leather weight can lead to: Stitches pulling through if it’s too thin. Difficulty folding or sewing if it’s too thick. A finished piece that doesn’t hold its shape over time. By matching the leather thickness to the function of your project, you get something that not only looks good but also lasts for years.

title: Jake Stolowski Featured in Modern Materials Handling’s Article
summary: The article features Matthews’ Jake Stolowski highlighting the advantages of light-directed batch picking carts
body_text: Matthews’ Jake Stolowski highlights the advantages of light-directed batch picking carts Modern Materials Handling provides comprehensive coverage of productivity solutions for materials handling professionals in distribution, warehousing and manufacturing. Their article “ Warehouse automation: Lights-directed picking carts boost productivity ” discuses the current warehousing landscape, and the emphasis on using high-tech solutions like AI and robotics to improve productivity. However, simpler and more affordable solutions can also significantly improve operations, especially since many warehouses are smaller and predominantly manual. For the article, writer Amanda Loudin interviewed Jake Stolowski, Senior Manager of Lighting Pick project management for Matthews Automation. Jake shared his perspective on why batch picking carts are an ideal entry point into automation. He also explains that these systems require very little infrastructure—just Wi-Fi and a host connection—and can be custom designed to fit SKU profiles and productivity goals. He also highlights the evolution of the technology: modern carts run on lightweight electric tool batteries instead of heavy car batteries, making them easier to use. Also, smart carts are now robust enough to operate in freezer environments, a growing need for 3PL providers serving meal delivery companies. Wi-Fi connectivity and adaptable hardware ensure the carts keep pace with changing warehouse demands. According to Stolowski, when implemented correctly, light-directed batch picking can increase productivity by about 40% and deliver nearly 100% picking accuracy compared to paper-based systems. The combination of scalability, fast ROI, and ease of adoption makes it one of the most accessible automation tools for facilities of all sizes. For more information, the entire “ Warehouse automation: Lights-directed picking carts boost productivity” article can be read here .
